key_concepts: Animals can be grouped as vertebrates or invertebrates based on characteristics.
Vertebrates are animals with a backbone.
Invertebrates are animals without a backbone.
Vertebrates include fish, birds, mammals, amphibians, and reptiles.
Fish have gills, fins, and scales and live in water.
Reptiles have dry scaly skin and are hatched from eggs.
Mammals have fur or hair, give birth to live young, and feed young with mammary glands.
Birds have wings, beaks, claws, and feathers and build nests.
Amphibians live on land and in water and have moist skin for breathing underwater.
Some invertebrates have an exoskeleton that supports and protects the body.
Animals can be classified by body support, breathing organs, and reproduction methods.
Protecting animals such as frogs and sea turtles is important for ecosystems.
